verses.zh: （大卫上行之诗。）耶和华啊，我的心不狂傲，我的眼不高大；重大和测不透的事，我也不敢行。
verses.en: A song of ascents,[NOTE:1] by David.O Lord, my heart is not proud,nor do I have a haughty look.[NOTE:2] I do not have great aspirations,or concern myself with things that are beyond me.[NOTE:3]
notes: Psalm 131. The psalmist affirms his humble dependence on the Lord and urges Israel to place its trust in God.

The precise significance of this title, which appears in Pss 120-134, is unclear. Perhaps worshipers recited these psalms when they ascended the road to Jerusalem to celebrate annual religious festivals. For a discussion of their background see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 219-21.
Heb “and my eyes are not lifted up.”
verses.commentary:
131:1 "Lord" This is the covenant name for Israel's Deity, first used in Genesis 2:4.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "heart" This is a Hebrew idiom referring to a person.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEART

▣ "not proud" The psalmist describes his humble attitude toward God in several phrases in Ps. 131:1-2.

- not proud (lit. "not lifted up") ‒ BDB 146, KB 170, Qal PERFECT

- eyes not haughty (lit. "my eyes not raised") ‒ BDB 926, KB 1202, Qal PERFECT

- do not involve (lit. "walk," BDB 229, KB 246, Piel PERFECT) myself in

- great matters (BDB 152)

- things too difficult (BDB 810, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: WONDERFUL THINGS) for me

- composed my soul ‒ BDB 1000, KB 1436, Piel PERFECT

- quieted my soul ‒ BDB 198, KB 226, Poel PERFECT

Proud and haughty people are the recipients of YHWH's wrath (cf. Ps. 18:27; 101:5; Zeph. 3:11)
because it reveals the results of the Fall of Genesis 3. Humility shows the results of a spiritual conversion and
acceptance of God's revelation.

There is a real question about what the imagery of #3 means.

- simply an idiom of humility

- simply an idiom of dependance

- someone who does not question God's great acts

- someone who does not presume on God's power

- a human who knows his/her place in the scheme of things (cf. Ps. 89:10)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

verses.zh: 我的心平稳安静，好像断过奶的孩子在他母亲的怀中；我的心在我里面真像断过奶的孩子。
verses.en: Indeed,[NOTE:1] I have calmed and quieted myself[NOTE:2] like a weaned child with its mother;[NOTE:3] I am content like a young child.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “I do not walk in great things, and in things too marvelous for me.”
Heb “I make level and make quiet my soul.”
Heb “like a weaned [one] upon his mother.”
verses.commentary:
131:2 The psalmist continues to describe his humble attitude by using the imagery of a child. Notice the
imagery is of YHWH as a mother.

- Gen. 1:2 ‒ the Spirit "brooded" (a FEMININE VERB)

- Deut. 32:11; Exod. 19:4 ‒ actions of female eagle

- the word Shaddai (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: SHADDAI)

- Isaiah 49:15; 66:9-13

- even Jesus used feminine images for Himself ‒ Matt. 23:37; Luke 13:34

For more information, listen to my sermon on Mother's Day, "The Femininity of God" online, second green box, #111;
www.freebiblecommentary.org

▣ "soul" This is nephesh (BDB 659), a way, like "heart," of referring to the whole person. See
full note at Gen. 35:18 online.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

verses.zh: 以色列啊，你当仰望耶和华，从今时直到永远！
verses.en: O Israel, hope in the Lordnow and forevermore!
verses.commentary:
131:3 The psalmist uses his own humble heart and peaceful hope/trust/patience (BDB 403, KB 407,
Piel IMPERATIVE, cf. Ps. 130:5,6,7) to encourage national Israel to the same place.

▣ "O, Israel" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

▣ "From this time forth and forever" This Hebrew idiom uses three words beginning with "ע"
(cf. Ps. 113:2; 115:18; 121:8; 125:2).

- BDB 773 ‒ ADVERB for current time (i.e., first phrase)

- BDB 723 III ‒ PREPOSITION

- BDB 761 ‒ IMPERATIVE, 'olam

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam)
